status: completed relevance and independent occurrence-evidence review

review.requirement_proposition: Appropriate mechanisms should allow AI systems risking undue harm or exhibiting unwanted behaviour to be safely overridden, repaired or decommissioned as needed.
review.reason_for_change: DeepSeek secured the exposed database after Wiz notified the company. That action repaired the reported public access state. The result covers closure of the exposure. It does not establish recovery of any data already accessed.

review.requirement_proposition: AI actors should respect the rule of law, human rights and democratic and human-centred values throughout the AI lifecycle, including non-discrimination, equality, freedom, dignity, individual autonomy, privacy and data protection, diversity, fairness, social justice and internationally recognised labour rights.
review.reason_for_change: Wiz directly accessed unauthenticated chat histories and secrets in DeepSeek’s database. Personal AI interaction data was publicly accessible without an access gate. That exposure did not preserve privacy and data protection. Earlier access by other parties remains unproved.

review.requirement_proposition: Delete the special-category personal data when the bias has been corrected or when the applicable retention period ends, whichever occurs first.

review.reason_for_change: Article 4a(1)(e) concerns exceptional bias-correction processing of special-category data. This operational chat-log database exposure does not identify that activity or its legal predicates.

conclusion_change.previous: The occurrence is a material AI-platform data-security failure in surrounding infrastructure rather than a model-behaviour failure. It demonstrates that governance of frontier AI services includes conventional but consequential access control, data custody and operational-security boundaries. Database reachability and exposed sensitive logs do not themselves show a governance process treating capability as permission. Notification and closure do not establish earlier third-party access, model-training exposure or runtime-agent admission.
conclusion_change.new: The occurrence is a material AI-platform data-security failure in surrounding infrastructure rather than a model-behaviour failure. It demonstrates that governance of frontier AI services includes conventional but consequential access control, data custody and operational-security boundaries. Database reachability and exposed sensitive logs do not themselves show a governance process treating capability as permission. Notification and closure do not establish earlier third-party access, model-training exposure or runtime-agent admission. The privacy and infrastructure-security outcomes are Not aligned. Closure of the unauthenticated exposure is Aligned with the repair requirement.
